title.narrative: Strengthening WASH Governance in Malawi – Phase Three

description.narrative: Direct Beneficiaries at Micro-Level: Water Point Committees; Dedza Waterpoints Area Mechanics Association (DWAMA);Spare Part Suppliers.Direct Beneficiaries at Meso-Level: District Water Development Office; District Environmental Health Office ; District Education Management Office; District Community Development Office; District Planning Department; District Environmental Office; Dedza WASH Chapter; Area Executive Committees.Direct Beneficiaries at Macro-Level: Ministry of Water and Sanitation; Ministry of Health; Ministry of Local Government.Indirect Beneficiaries at Micro-Level: Traditional Authorities; Individual households; Area mechanics.Indirect Beneficiaries at Meso-Level that are not directly benefiting: (International) WASH NGOs operating in Dedza District. Indirect Beneficiaries at Macro-Level that are not directly benefiting: (International) WASH NGOs operating in Malawi.WHO and UNICEF offices at the global level; Other country government representatives.

Outcome 1: Macro (National). The WASH system is strengthened at the national level, and systems-based approaches to WASH programming are upscaled.Outcome 2: Meso-Level (District). WASH governance in Dedza District is strengthened.Outcome 3: Micro-Level (community, service provider and household). The Dedza Waterpoints Area Mechanics Association (DWAMA) is able to discharge its duties sustainably.
This is the third phase of WASH-SSI project in Malawi. Together with two partners (WESNET and BASEDA) the project aims to support WASH governance at national and district level (Dedza).
